items.question: Can a score ever fall?
At what dice spread do races stop resolving on the tally, and does race-flip diverge from winner-flip?
items.notRun: the 3d6 spread is not a config knob; `zeroDiceWinner` gives the 0x point and nothing gives 0.25x, 0.5x or 2x. Report both share of races resolving differently AND share of games with a different winner when it is built: high race-flip with low winner-flip is the healthy shape.

items.question: Does the engine produce a Skowronekian regime — settlement, strain, disjunction?
items.notRun: built and run separately: `npm run skowronek`. Read era-check 1 first — if settlement position random-walks with no persistent regime, nothing else in the suite means anything. As of v0.2 its two construction-level preconditions (BILL_CORPUS, BILL_POSITION) are MET; STRAIN_RISE and EFFICACY_DROP are now ABSENT rather than ABSENT_BY_CONSTRUCTION, i.e. unbuilt rather than unbuildable.

items.question: Is the presidency the game? A committee operator should be able to win without it.

measures.name: r2 of final score on presidential years

items.verdict: top scorer lacks the presidency in 27% of games (target >=30%); presidential years explain r2=0.29 of final score (target <0.50)

items.question: Does the board produce split-ticket voting — a state going one way at the top and another below it?

measures.name: mean gap
measures.historicalNote: all fifty states, every presidential cycle 1976-2016, from pres_state_panel.json and house_district_panel.json. Same definition both sides — the test program's SPEC one, top-of-ticket party's House share subtracted from 100. NOTE the source disagrees with itself: the worked table in the test program is keyed on the REPUBLICAN share in every row, which is a different quantity once the top of the ticket flips. On 1976 the two readings give 24.9pp and 75.1pp, and only the R-keyed one supports the table's "reversed" note.

measures.name: share of state-cycles above 69pp
measures.historicalNote: same population and same definition as the row above. For scale, the five Deep South states the test program tracks average 42.2pp over the same period — the extreme case the design is aimed at. There is no engine counterpart to that row, because the engine plays all fifty, so it is quoted here rather than measured.

measures.name: precondition: presidential-year state-cells with no House seat

items.verdict: mean gap 49.1pp against 39.0pp in the returns (all fifty states, 1976-2016); band 20-59pp. 45% of state-cycles clear 69pp against 14% historically; band 7-28%. The mean is inside the record and the tail is not: the board produces divergence of about the right average size and far too many extreme cases.

items.question: Does a district ever change its vehicle while keeping its interest?
items.verdict: 5% of consecutive holds change party against 5% changing interest — ratio 1.0 (target >=2). NOTE: candidate tag-fit is measured against the district a card actually ran in, so a district with no card in play contributes nothing.

items.question: Do concentration and diversity beat each other conditionally, or is the ladder perfectly transitive?
items.notRun: the duel matrix is `node sim/roundrobin.ts`, not re-run here. Acceptance: the matrix must NOT be perfectly transitive on both configs, and must include hand-written adversarial strategies designed to beat the top — if nothing in a reasonable strategy space beats it, that is structural. `WideAndEmpty` at 0.0% of every duel is the v0.1.2 reading.

items.question: Does the president's party lose ground at the midterm, as it did in every postwar cycle but two?

measures.name: president's party loses seat share at the midterm
measures.historicalNote: 9 of 11 midterms 1978-2018 in house_district_panel.json; the two exceptions the data finds are 1998 and 2002, which are the two the record names. Same quantity both sides: share of House seats held by the president's party, against the previous election.

measures.name: historical band, lower (Wilson 95% on the record)
historical band, upper (Wilson 95% on the record)

items.verdict: 53% of midterms cost the president's party ground, against 81.8% in the returns (9 of 11, 1978-2018, the exceptions being 1998 and 2002). Band is the Wilson 95% interval on that: 52-95%. Derived from house_district_panel.json, not chosen.

items.verdict: the cap is 16 years against a 30-40 year reference regime; below 30 a null settlement result is a fact about the clock

items.question: How long does the board take to turn lean into seats?

measures.name: median years from lean crossing to delegation flip
measures.historicalNote: the Deep South turned at the top of the ticket in 1964 and its House delegation went majority-R in 1996, per house_district_panel.json — a 32-year lag. The lean date is documented rather than derived: the panel starts in 1976 and the turn is outside it. NOT like-for-like on the clock: a game is 16 years, so a 32-year lag cannot occur in one, and the engine figure is bounded by the cap rather than by the rules.

measures.name: lean crossings that reached a delegation flip
Deep South R House share, first panel year
Deep South R House share, last panel year

items.verdict: median lag 0 years against 32 in the record (1964 lean -> 1996 delegation). The bar is >=8 years, a quarter of the historical figure, because a 16-year cap cannot contain 32 and grading against the full figure would grade the clock. See D4.
